subject: Discovery recap — cost levers, budget guardrails, next actions
messages:
From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@payzen.co>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Claire Summers <claire@payzen.co>
Date: 2027-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap from today

Jonas / team — thanks for the call today. Wanted to put the key constraints in writing so we’ve got alignment on scope: 

- Pain: inference spend is the single fastest-growing line item for our recommendations feature. We’re seeing monthly spend spikes and unpredictable per-invoice increases.
- Goals: keep latency under 400ms p95 for user-facing recs, reduce monthly inference spend while keeping model quality ~same, and have predictable monthly spend for forecasting.
- Budget guardrail: we can allocate up to $15k/month for a proof-of-concept (pilot) but need a clear ROI story to expand.
- Usage profile: roughly 80 QPS at peak, median prompt ~120 tokens in, 40 tokens output. (We’ll attach a small sample log.)

Open asks: can you outline the main cost levers (batching, caching, model variants, quantization) and a realistic TCO range for a 30-day pilot? Also want a plain-English summary of what the pilot would prove.

Claire and I can share anonymized request logs and a short runbook for security review.

—Ethan
Product Lead, Recommendations
PayZen

Attachments: payzen-sample-logs.json (see drive link)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@payzen.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T16:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today

Ethan — thanks for writing this up and for sharing the numbers on the call. Short recap and the direct answers to your asks below. I attached a short KPI sheet and our discovery notes.

Recap of pain & objective (agree):
- High monthly variance on inference costs; forecasting difficulty.
- Need to keep user-facing latency p95 <= 400ms.
- Pilot budget constraint: ~ $15k/mo cap — must show 3–6x ROI to move to a larger commit.

Primary cost levers we recommend to hit those constraints:
1) Batching + adaptive batching windows — for your 80 QPS peak and 120-token inputs we'll typically see 25–35% token-cost reduction without breaching 400ms p95 if windows are tuned to traffic shape.
2) Prefix (KV) caching — if recommendation prompts reuse product-context prefixes we can often reduce repeated compute for cached prefixes (30–60% savings on repeated workflows).
3) Model variant + quantization — run heavier model for quality-critical requests and a 4-bit quantized variant for standard requests; combined routing reduces cost per token by ~35–50% depending on quality split.
4) Smart routing & regional placement — route less latency-sensitive rerank/batch work to cheaper regions / capacity tiers.

Ballpark pilot TCO scenarios (30 days) — estimates for planning only:
- Conservative: $11k (small batch tuning, no quantization)
- Mid: $8.5k (batching + caching tuned, mixed model split)
- Optimistic: $5.5k (aggressive caching + quantized routing on 60% of calls)

What the pilot proves:
- Realized cost per 1M tokens under your traffic shape and quality constraints
- Latency SLO compliance with suggested batching windows
- Operational workflows needed for rollout (monitoring, rollback, space for Dedicated if needed)

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share a 48-hour sample of anonymized logs (Claire/Ethan) — drives the simulator and gives us a realistic projection.
2) Redwood runs a 5-day simulated run and returns a short TCO report + recommended config.
3) If numbers look good, we scope a 14–30 day pilot (we can target May 5 kickoff) with clear success metrics (cost delta, p95 latency).

I’ve attached: payzen-discovery-notes.pdf and sample-kpi-sheet.xlsx. Marissa / Ben — adding you for pilot scoping and ops plan.

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@payzen.co>
Date: 2027-04-22T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today — pilot operational notes

Adding a few operational points on the pilot scope:

- Canaries & guardrails: we should start the pilot with 5–10% traffic canary to validate latency and quality before increasing load. Clear kill-switch conditions: sustained p95 > 500ms or unexpected error rate > 1.5%.
- Observability: we’ll provide route-level token and latency dashboards and a daily snapshot during the pilot.
- Dedicated vs Hosted: if PayZen expects consistent QPS with tight SLOs, Dedicated capacity pricing may be better after the pilot; we’ll include a brief comparison in the TCO report.
- Inputs we need from PayZen: QPS by hour (sample 48h), percent of requests that reuse a product prefix (cacheability estimate), and three example prompts for qualitative check.

I attached pilot-cost-scenarios.xlsx with simple cost buckets (batching savings, caching delta, model-split outcomes) so Ethan/Claire can see sensitivity to cache hit rate and quantization share.

Marissa Cole
Product Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Summers <claire@payzen.co>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@payzen.co>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today

Thanks — this is great, thanks for the clear options. Per your request, attached are a 48-hour sample (anonymized), a short doc with cacheability indicators, and our preferred pilot window. A few clarifications from our side:

- We confirm pilot budget max $15k/month; interested in aiming for the mid scenario but want the conservative case spelled out for Finance.
- Cacheability: roughly 42% of calls reuse a product-context prefix.
- Token distribution: median prompt 120 tokens in / 40 out; 95th percentile tokens ~ 410 total.
- Suggested kickoff: May 5 (can do a 14-day pilot first, extend if results are promising).

We’ve uploaded the sample logs to the Drive link you sent. Please let us know if you need the security questionnaire filled before the pilot starts — our InfoSec team will want that.

Claire Summers
Head of Data Products | PayZen
